course.title: A Different World: Black Experience and American Society

outcomes.LO1: Apply core sociological frameworks to a single sustained case across 39 years
outcomes.LO2: Analyse how a commercial entertainment text encodes, contests and reproduces racial ideology
outcomes.LO3: Use double consciousness and its refinements to analyse identity as structure and meaning-making
outcomes.LO4: Evaluate empirical claims about Black life and distinguish structural accounts from deficit narratives
outcomes.LO5: Write sociological analysis for a non-specialist audience with citations
outcomes.LO6: Connect a Black-specific case to general social theory

sessions.title: What A Different World Is: Hillman as a Sociological Object
sessions.big_question: What kind of social object is a television series, and what does it take to read one sociologically?

sessions.title: Voice, Censorship, and the Student as Political Actor
sessions.big_question: When a student speaks and an institution answers, what is being negotiated?

sessions.title: Homecoming, Ritual, and Collective Identity
sessions.big_question: What does ritual do for a community, and what does it hide?

sessions.title: Intimacy, Gender, and the Script of Romance
sessions.big_question: Is romance personal or structural — and what changes when both are true?
concepts: mate selection and the marriage market

sessions.title: Crisis, Care, and the Sociology of Health
sessions.big_question: Why did a Black sitcom put an HIV diagnosis on prime time in 1991, and what does a crisis mean on television now?

originals.title: If I Should Die Before I Wake

concepts: the sitcom as public health intervention

sessions.title: Generation, Memory, and 'the Aunties'
sessions.big_question: How is a generation made, and who does the work of holding one together?

sessions.title: Diaspora: Who Belongs to the 'Black Experience'?
sessions.big_question: What is at stake when a category that looks unified is contested from inside?
sessions.episode_title: Sometimes You Get the Culture...Sometimes the Culture Gets You (first half)

sessions.title: Pageants, Colourism, and Hierarchy Inside Black Space
sessions.big_question: How does stratification work inside a group that is itself stratified against?
sessions.episode_title: Sometimes You Get the Culture...Sometimes the Culture Gets You (second half)

sessions.title: Storm, Confinement, and the Conflict We Avoid
sessions.big_question: What does forced proximity do to a relationship, and what does the scene reveal about disclosure?

originals.title: In the Eye of the Storm

sessions.title: Budgets, Institutions, and Racialized Organizations
sessions.big_question: What is an institution for, and what happens when the money runs out?

originals.title: Take This Job and Love It

sessions.title: The Finale as Argument: What Survives
sessions.big_question: What is a season finale arguing about an institution's future?

sessions.title: Media, Image, and the Politics of Representation
sessions.big_question: Who controls the image, and what does an image do to the people it depicts?

sessions.title: Family, Class, and the 'Culture' Question
sessions.big_question: When inequality is explained by culture, what is being explained — and what is being excused?
concepts: the Moynihan debate and its critics

sessions.title: The State, the Street, and the Ledger
sessions.big_question: How did a family sitcom put an uprising in its season premiere — and where is that tradition now?

sessions.title: Capstone: The Black Experience Is American Society
sessions.big_question: If the case is American, what follows for how the discipline tells its story?

originals.title: A Rock, a River, a Lena
